Legions Imperialis Miniature Scale for 3D Printing

Legions Imperialis is Games Workshop's modern 8mm epic scale, where Titans and massed infantry share a table. It shares its scale with Adeptus Titanicus, but the two use different bases, so scaling a file correctly for one does not automatically mean it fits the other.

Legions Imperialis uses 8mm scale, matching the older Adeptus Titanicus range. The scale is designed so that a Titan miniature is roughly the same physical size as a 28mm infantry model, creating an intentionally dramatic size contrast on the table.

Publisher: Games Workshop·Base Sizes: Hex and movement-tray based

The big draw for FDM is the Titans and large vehicles, which are excellent subjects and print cleanly. The smaller infantry is the hard part — at 8mm it is manageable but rough, and I keep my expectations realistic about what a hobby nozzle can hold.

The base-size difference between Legions Imperialis and Adeptus Titanicus is a real trap. I confirm the footprint for the specific game before scaling so my print sits on the right base rather than needing a re-scale after the fact.

Deep Dive: 8mm epic — Titans next to 28mm infantry

Legions Imperialis is 8mm, tuned so a Titan is roughly the physical size of a 28mm infantry model. That dramatic contrast is the point — and it means you should never 'fix' it by scaling up.

The 8mm Epic Scale

Legions Imperialis is 8mm scale (1:200), matching the older Adeptus Titanicus range. Individual Space Marines are tiny but recognizable, and massed formations of hundreds of models fit on a single table. It is Games Workshop's return to epic-scale warfare, set during the Horus Heresy.

The Contrast Is Intentional

The scale is designed so a Titan miniature is roughly the same physical size as a 28mm infantry model. That size contrast between the tiny Marine line and the looming Titans is the whole point of the game — do not scale a Titan up "so it feels big." Also, Legions Imperialis and Adeptus Titanicus share the scale but not the base sizes, so keep the bases straight when you print replacements.

FDM for the Big Stuff, Skip the Infantry

At 8mm, infantry is beyond what FDM can reliably produce — the minis come out as blobs. Vehicles and Titans are larger and more forgiving, and FDM handles them fine. I print the machines at 0.2mm nozzle and 0.04mm layers. For painting at this size, contrast paints and washes beat layer-by-layer highlighting every time.

Common Legions Imperialis Mistakes

  • FDM on the infantry. 8mm Marines come out as blobs — print the vehicles and Titans instead.
  • Scaling Titans up for drama. The scale contrast is the design. Leave the numbers alone.
  • Confusing Legions Imperialis and Adeptus Titanicus bases. Same scale, different base sizes — print to the right one for the game you play.

Printing these minis on FDM

Titans and large vehicles print great on FDM. The 8mm infantry is manageable at a fine profile. Confirm the correct base size for your specific epic-scale game before scaling.

All settings tested on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini with PLA. Your printer may want something different — always print a test piece first.
